records.abstract_pattern: This pattern summarizes a period's performance by presenting a list of key achievements across different business dimensions. It anchors on a major milestone or qualitative achievement (like reaching profitability) and supports it with a series of strong quantitative metrics (like revenue growth, margin improvement, and operational velocity). Any company can use this to create a powerful 'state of the union' slide that proves the business is healthy and executing well on multiple fronts, demonstrating both financial discipline and growth momentum.
works_for: We've hit 1 million active users while also becoming cash-flow positive.
Our new product line already contributes 20% of revenue and has industry-leading engagement.
We successfully expanded into Europe, which is now our fastest-growing region, while improving overall company margins.
We achieved record user growth this quarter and simultaneously reduced our customer acquisition cost by 30%.
Our platform is now the market leader in our category, supported by record sales and top-tier customer logos.
We've reached a key product milestone by shipping our V2, which has already doubled user retention rates.
Our shift to enterprise has been a success, with enterprise ARR growing 50% while the sales cycle shortened.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A headline achievement or milestone (e.g., profitability, market leadership, major product launch).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A list of supporting quantitative metrics (e.g., revenue growth, user growth, margins, sales velocity).
variable_elements.time_dimension: Point-in-time summary for a specific period (e.g., quarter, year) with year-over-year comparisons.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time (Year-over-Year).

must_have: A major company milestone to announce (e.g., first-time profitability, market share leadership)
Several supporting KPIs from different areas (e.g., finance, sales, operations, product)
Data for the current period and the prior year period for comparison
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: A collection of strong, positive metrics across different functions, ideally showing both growth and efficiency.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 1 headline achievement and 3-5 supporting metrics.

ideal_for: Summarizing quarterly or annual performance for investors or the board.
Announcing a major inflection point, like achieving profitability or cash-flow breakeven.
Kicking off a presentation with a strong executive summary of recent success.
Demonstrating balanced growth, showing both top-line momentum and bottom-line discipline.
When you have good news across multiple parts of the business (e.g., sales, finance, product).
Proving the business model is working at scale.
avoid_when: When you only have one good metric to share, as this format relies on breadth.
When performance is mixed or negative; a different format is needed to explain challenges.
When you need to do a deep-dive analysis of a single metric.

Customer count data
A sales activity metric (e.g., deals closed, bookings)
A profitability or efficiency metric (e.g., operating margin, EBITDA, CAC)

ideal_for: Providing a high-level summary of a successful quarter or year.
Opening an investor update or all-hands meeting to set a positive tone.
Demonstrating that growth is balanced and not reliant on a single factor.
Establishing credibility by showing strong performance across the board.
When you need a 'brag slide' to summarize overall business health.
Summarizing performance before a deep-dive into a specific area.

When you need to tell a deep-dive story about a single metric's trend over time.
If your key metrics are stagnant or declining.

records.abstract_pattern: Any company can use this pattern to showcase a dramatic transformation enabled by their product, using a powerful third-party endorsement as the primary evidence. The slide structure combines a quote from a credible authority with a 'before and after' visual to make the value proposition tangible. This pattern emphasizes not just the scale of the transformation (from simple/manual to complex/automated) but also the incredible speed ('time to value') at which it was achieved, proving the product's power and efficiency in a mission-critical context.
works_for: A major bank went from manual fraud detection to real-time AI-powered prevention in one month using our platform.
We helped a global retailer unify 50 disparate inventory systems into a single source of truth in just 8 weeks.
Our marketing automation tool took a CPG brand from batch-and-blast emails to personalized journeys, doubling engagement in a quarter.
A leading pharma company used our software to cut their drug discovery analysis time from 6 months to 2 weeks.

Our platform enabled a logistics giant to move from quarterly network planning to real-time route optimization.
A government agency used our product to consolidate hundreds of databases into a single, queryable intelligence platform in under a month.

variable_elements.primary_metric: The sophisticated 'after' state (e.g., comprehensive analysis, unified dashboard, real-time system).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: The simplistic 'before' state (e.g., simple spreadsheet, manual process, disparate systems).
variable_elements.time_dimension: The rapid timeframe of the transformation (e.g., 'in weeks', 'in one month').
variable_elements.comparison_basis: A single entity's process before and after product adoption, validated by an external expert.

must_have: A powerful, attributable quote from a credible, high-profile customer or external expert.
A clear 'before' state that is simple or problematic.
A clear 'after' state enabled by the product that is sophisticated and valuable.
A specific, short timeframe for the transformation.
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: needs_clear_contrast
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 1 strong case study with a willing and credible reference.

ideal_for: Establishing credibility with skeptical enterprise buyers or investors.
Proving rapid time-to-value and ease of implementation for a complex product.
Demonstrating the product's ability to solve mission-critical, large-scale problems.
Justifying a premium price point by showing transformative impact.
Highlighting a 'lighthouse' customer success story to attract similar clients.
Opening a presentation section focused on customer proof or real-world impact.
avoid_when: You do not have a strong, quotable, and credible customer endorsement.
The 'before and after' story shows only incremental improvement, not transformation.
Your product's implementation time is long, as this pattern emphasizes speed.

variable_elements.secondary_metric: A conceptual framework (Venn diagram, flywheel, etc.) explaining the partnership model.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicitly vs. competitors (by naming a 'differentiator').

must_have: A strong, quotable testimonial from a credible, named customer (with title and company)
Permission to use the customer's name and logo
A conceptual framework that explains how value is created through partnership

ideal_for: When you need to prove a specific technical feature is a major competitive advantage.
To add social proof and credibility from a recognized industry leader.
When explaining a complex value proposition that involves both technology and services/partnership.
To showcase a flagship customer success story in a concise, powerful way.
When you want to shift the narrative from what your product *is* to what it *achieves* with a customer.
avoid_when: You don't have permission from a credible customer to be featured.
Your best testimonials are generic and don't point to a specific differentiator.
Your business model is purely transactional and self-service with no partnership element.

records.title: Products launched at FoundryCon US 2023

records.core_message: Our platform now includes a powerful Process Mining & Automation Suite that enables customers to visualize, analyze, and optimize their complex business processes to uncover and fix inefficiencies.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern explains a complex product or process using a multi-step, conceptual diagram alongside a concise text description. It breaks down a sophisticated capability into digestible, sequential stages to make it understandable. Any company can use this when they need to explain *how* their product achieves a specific outcome, moving from an abstract problem to a concrete solution. This approach builds credibility by making the abstract 'magic' of the technology tangible and visually mapping the path to value.
works_for: Our AI-powered marketing platform automates campaign creation from audience segmentation to ad deployment.
Our security software identifies threats by analyzing network traffic, isolating anomalies, and neutralizing them in real-time.
Our supply chain solution provides end-to-end visibility from raw material sourcing to final delivery.

Our drug discovery platform accelerates research by simulating molecular interactions and predicting compound efficacy.
Our system turns unstructured customer feedback into actionable product insights through a three-step process.
This is how our platform creates a 'digital twin' of a customer's factory to optimize production.

variable_elements.primary_metric: Process Stages

must_have: A clear, multi-step process for how a product or service works
A defined value proposition or outcome that the process delivers (e.g., 'find inefficiencies', 'automate campaigns')

ideal_for: Explaining a new, complex product or feature to investors or customers.
Illustrating 'how the magic happens' for a technologically sophisticated solution.
Breaking down a value chain or workflow into understandable steps.
Justifying a premium price point by showcasing the underlying complexity and power.
Differentiating from simpler competitors by highlighting a more comprehensive process.
Visually explaining the architecture of a software platform.
avoid_when: The product or process is very simple and self-explanatory.
The primary goal is to show quantitative results (e.g., revenue growth), not how something works.
The audience is non-technical and only needs the high-level benefit, not the process details.

It shows categories like Data Types (Sensor, ERP, Financial), Model Types (Physics, Financial, Scheduling), and Application Layers (Analytics, Workflows, Integrations). records.abstract_pattern: Any company with a complex platform can use this pattern to illustrate its technical architecture and value chain. The slide visually deconstructs the system into layers, starting with diverse, raw inputs (like data sources or models), processing them through a central, proprietary engine (the 'secret sauce'), and culminating in high-value applications and actions. This 'input-process-output' stack diagram effectively communicates technical depth, integration capabilities, and how the platform creates tangible outcomes from complexity.
works_for: Our ad platform turns raw user signals into optimized, real-time campaign decisions.
Our drug discovery engine translates genomic data into validated therapeutic targets.
Our supply chain OS creates a digital twin from disparate logistics data to automate routing.
Our security fabric correlates telemetry from across the enterprise to neutralize threats automatically.
Our financial platform aggregates market and transaction data to power automated risk management tools.
We provide a complete operating system for the modern factory, from sensor data to production scheduling.
Our marketing cloud integrates customer data points into a single view to enable personalized journeys.

variable_elements.primary_metric: Core Proprietary Layer (e.g., Ontology, Identity Graph, Digital Twin)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: Input & Output Layers (e.g., Data Sources, Applications)
variable_elements.time_dimension: None, it's a static architecture diagram.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicitly compares an integrated platform against siloed point solutions.

must_have: A well-defined product architecture with distinct layers
A list of input data sources or foundational elements
A central, proprietary processing or integration concept
A set of high-level applications or use cases enabled by the platform
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a layered or tiered structure showing a clear flow from foundational inputs to high-level outputs.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: At least 3 layers (e.g., inputs, core processing, outputs) with 3-5 examples in each layer.

ideal_for: Explaining a complex, multi-layered product to a sophisticated audience.
Demonstrating a strong technical moat that competitors cannot easily replicate.
Justifying a high price point by showing the depth of the solution.
In a product-focused section of an investor deck to showcase innovation.
Differentiating from simpler point solutions by highlighting integration capabilities.
Onboarding new enterprise clients to explain how the system works.
avoid_when: Your product is a simple, single-purpose tool.
Presenting to a non-technical audience that needs a high-level value proposition.
Your platform architecture is not yet well-defined or is in flux.

We are moving from a product to a platform, creating an ecosystem for our customers.

variable_elements.primary_metric: New Capability (e.g., Developer Suite, API, SDK, Marketplace)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicitly, the product's past self (product vs. platform)

must_have: A new, significant feature or program that enables customers/users to build or create on your platform.
A clear name for this new capability.
A concise explanation of its value proposition to the user/developer.

data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 1 new major capability announcement

ideal_for: Announcing a strategic shift from a closed product to an open platform.
Demonstrating a new, powerful competitive moat that is hard to replicate.
Explaining a future growth driver beyond core product sales.
Showcasing product maturity and a vision for an ecosystem.
Justifying higher valuation by showing potential for network effects.

The product is a simple, single-purpose tool, not a foundational platform.

This structure provides clarity and helps the audience follow the narrative arc of the presentation, acting as a 'chapter heading' in the story.

The title of the upcoming section

Starting a new 'chapter' in the company's story during a pitch.
Enhancing the professionalism and structure of a formal presentation.
avoid_when: In a very short, informal update (e.g., a 3-slide presentation).

In a rapid-fire pitch where every second counts and transitions are verbal.

Any company can use this to spotlight strong performance in a core metric (like revenue or users) or a specific segment of that metric, providing a clear and powerful snapshot of positive momentum.

Our enterprise customer count has more than doubled in the past year.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A key performance indicator (e.g., Revenue, Users, Customers, ARR, Profit).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: The percentage growth rate of the primary metric.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time.

The absolute value for both periods
The calculated percentage growth between the periods

ideal_for: Highlighting strong year-over-year growth in a core financial or operational metric.

Showcasing the strength and momentum of a particular business segment or geography.
Opening a financial update to immediately establish a narrative of positive momentum.
When you want to communicate both impressive scale (the big number) and rapid growth (the percentage).
In an investor or board update to prove the business is scaling effectively.

When the absolute numbers are not yet impressive on their own (e.g., very early stage).

records.abstract_pattern: Any company can use this pattern to demonstrate the health and diversification of its growth by breaking down a key metric (like revenue or user growth) into its primary segments. This visual effectively communicates that the company has multiple engines for growth and is successfully expanding its addressable market or product appeal.
works_for: Our enterprise revenue is accelerating, complementing our stable SMB base.
International user growth is now outpacing our domestic growth.
While our hardware sales are steady, our high-margin software subscriptions are growing exponentially.

Our self-serve customer base is growing at 3x the rate of our managed accounts.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A key performance indicator, such as Revenue, Users, or Bookings.
variable_elements.secondary_metric: The percentage growth rate of the primary metric.

A clear way to segment that data (e.g., by customer type, geography, product line)

To re-frame a narrative of slowing overall growth by highlighting rapid growth in a key strategic area.
When reporting financial results to investors, breaking down performance by division.
To justify increased investment in a newer, high-growth part of the business.
To show you are successfully de-risking the business by diversifying revenue streams.
avoid_when: When all your segments are growing at roughly the same rate, as the story is less impactful.
If your new/expansion segment is not growing or is negligibly small.
If you only have one business segment.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A key performance indicator, such as Revenue, Users, or Customers.
variable_elements.secondary_metric: The growth rate (e.g., YoY percentage) of the primary metric.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Comparison between internal business segments.

records.core_message: We are achieving significant and sustained revenue growth at scale, which is underpinned by a healthy business model proven by strong customer retention and expansion.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern demonstrates strong business performance by pairing a primary growth metric with a key underlying driver. This combination proves not just that the company is growing, but that the growth is healthy, sustainable, and driven by a strong core business model.

We grew bookings by 35% this year while simultaneously reducing customer acquisition cost by 15%.
Our marketplace liquidity has tripled, with the average time-to-fill for an order dropping by 50%.
We hit $100M in revenue this year, a 75% increase, because customers are expanding their usage across more departments.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A key top-line metric (e.g., Revenue, ARR, GMV, Users)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A supporting driver KPI (e.g., Net Dollar Retention, Virality, Churn, ARPU)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time

A key performance indicator that explains or supports the growth story (e.g., net dollar retention)

Demonstrating the health and scalability of a SaaS or subscription-based business model.

When you want to communicate a key financial highlight simply and powerfully.
Proving that your growth isn't just from new sales but also from existing happy customers.
avoid_when: When growth has slowed, is flat, or is negative.
If you don't have a strong supporting KPI to explain the growth, as it would weaken the narrative.
For very early-stage companies where absolute numbers are small and YoY percentages can be misleading.

variable_elements.time_dimension: Time series, typically quarterly or monthly.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time.

Data for at least 5 consecutive periods to establish a clear trend

As a foundational slide in a financial or operating metrics section.

records.title: CUSTOMER COUNT

variable_elements.primary_metric: A measure of overall base growth (e.g., total customers, total users, number of logos).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A measure of value expansion within a key cohort (e.g., revenue per top customer, usage per enterprise user, average contract value).
variable_elements.time_dimension: Time-series, typically shown over several quarters or years.

Highlighting the health of an enterprise sales motion.
Building a case for strong net revenue retention.

If your new customer growth has stalled, making the 'land' part of the story weak.
If your business is purely transactional with no recurring or expansion revenue component.

Our marketplace is seeing more transactions and a higher Gross Merchandise Value (GMV).

variable_elements.primary_metric: A volume or activity metric (e.g., deals closed, customers acquired, active users).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A financial value metric (e.g., billings, revenue, ARPU, ACV).
variable_elements.time_dimension: Comparison between two distinct time periods (e.g., year-over-year, quarter-over-quarter).
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time.

must_have: A volume-based metric (e.g., deal count, customer count) for at least two comparable periods.
A value-based metric (e.g., billings, revenue) for the same two periods.
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs an upward trend in both metrics to be effective.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 2 time periods for two different metrics.

ideal_for: Demonstrating strong, healthy business momentum at the start of a financial update.
Showing that growth is coming from both new business volume and increasing deal value.
Providing leading indicators for future revenue growth (billings and deals are precursors to revenue).
Justifying sales and marketing investment by showing tangible results.
Building investor confidence in the company's growth story and execution.
Highlighting top-line performance in an annual or quarterly business review.
avoid_when: When one or both metrics are flat or declining.

When the primary message is about profitability or efficiency, not top-line growth.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A total count of a key activity (e.g., deals closed, users acquired, items processed).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: Subsets of the primary metric, filtered by increasing value thresholds (e.g., deal size, user type, transaction value).
variable_elements.time_dimension: A specific point in time or a recent period (e.g., 'Last Quarter', 'In 2023').
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicitly comparing the size of the subsets to the total, showing a distribution of value.

must_have: A list of transactions or events from a specific time period (e.g., deals closed, customers signed).
A value or tier associated with each transaction/event (e.g., contract value, user subscription tier, company size).
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a distribution with a sufficient quantity of high-value items to highlight. A power-law or long-tail distribution is ideal.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: At least one headline metric and two sub-metrics to show a meaningful breakdown.

ideal_for: When you need to prove you're moving upmarket and closing larger enterprise deals.
To demonstrate the quality and value distribution within your customer base or revenue.
To add substance to a headline sales number to show it's not just a vanity metric.
When highlighting sales team success in an investor update or company all-hands.
To show momentum in landing 'whale' customers or users.
When your average deal size is skewed by a few very large deals.
avoid_when: When all your deals or customers are roughly the same small size.
When you have very few deals in total, making the breakdown seem insignificant.
When your headline number is weak, as breaking it down will only emphasize the weakness.

records.title: DEALS CLOSED

records.core_message: Our business model is fundamentally strong and profitable, demonstrated by consistently high and stable gross margins above 80%.

shows.specific_content: A line chart showing Adjusted Gross Margin percentage over the four quarters of 2022. The line shows slight fluctuation but remains at a high level.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern showcases a key performance metric that is already at a high, best-in-class level and is maintaining that level over time. It's used to prove fundamental business model strength, stability, and efficiency, rather than showing rapid growth or improvement from a low base. Any company can use this to demonstrate that a core efficiency or quality metric is consistently excellent, proving the underlying health and defensibility of their operations. The minor fluctuations ending on a high note reinforce resilience.
works_for: Our software has best-in-class gross margins, proving our pricing power and efficient delivery.
We maintain industry-leading customer retention rates above 95% quarter after quarter.
Our platform uptime has been consistently above 99.99% for the past two years.
Our Net Promoter Score has remained in the top decile for our industry, showing sustained customer satisfaction.
Our contribution margin per transaction is stable and high, proving the long-term viability of our marketplace.
Our user engagement, measured by DAU/MAU, has been consistently high, proving product stickiness.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A key efficiency, quality, or satisfaction metric, typically a percentage (e.g., Gross Margin, Retention Rate, Uptime, NPS).
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time, with an implicit comparison to a high industry benchmark.

must_have: Time-series data for a key percentage-based KPI (e.g., gross margin, retention rate).
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a consistently high value (e.g., >75% for gross margin, >90% for retention) with only minor fluctuations to demonstrate stability.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 4+ time periods (e.g., quarters) to establish a pattern of consistency.

ideal_for: Proving the fundamental health and profitability of your business model.
Showing investors that high growth is not at the expense of core profitability.
Demonstrating a moat, as consistently high margins are hard for competitors to replicate.
Reassuring stakeholders about business stability during volatile periods.
Justifying a premium valuation based on best-in-class unit economics.
Highlighting a core strength in a mature, public company narrative.
avoid_when: Your margins or key metric are low or highly volatile.
You are pre-product-market fit and still establishing your cost structure.
The metric is trending downwards without a clear story of recovery or strategic reason.

records.title: Adjusted Gross Margin

records.core_message: We have a fortress-like balance sheet with billions in cash, no debt, and significant available credit, which is sustained by our strong positive cash flow.

shows.specific_content: A split-screen layout. The left side highlights a large cash balance ($2.6B) with no debt and an available credit facility ($950M). The right side shows a bar chart comparing FY 2022 Adjusted Free Cash Flow ($203M) and Cash from Operations ($224M).
shows.data_points_shown: Cash on hand: $2.6B. Debt: $0. Undrawn credit facility: $950M. FY 2022 Adjusted Free Cash Flow: $203M. FY 2022 Cash from Operations: $224M.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern establishes overwhelming financial strength by combining a headline 'fortress balance sheet' statement with supporting evidence of cash generation. It uses a large, memorable number (e.g., cash on hand, no debt) to anchor the message of stability and de-risking. This is then substantiated with a chart showing the underlying operational health (e.g., positive cash flow), proving that the strong balance sheet is not a one-time event but the result of a sustainable business model. Any company can use this to shift the narrative from 'are they viable?' to 'they are a stable, long-term player'.
works_for: We have over 5 years of runway at our current burn rate, giving us ample time to execute our strategy.
Our strong cash position allows us to invest aggressively in R&D and M&A while our competitors are cutting back.
We are fully funded to profitability and have no need to raise additional capital.
Our business model is inherently cash-generative, as shown by our consistent free cash flow.
We've built a resilient business with zero debt and a massive cash cushion to weather any market.
Our capital efficiency is a key competitive advantage that provides strategic flexibility.
We have achieved self-sufficiency and are no longer reliant on external capital markets.

variable_elements.primary_metric: Cash on hand / Balance sheet strength metric
variable_elements.secondary_metric: Cash flow metric (e.g., FCF, OCF)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Comparison of two related cash flow metrics

must_have: End-of-period cash balance
Total debt amount
Annual cash from operations
Annual free cash flow
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a large cash balance, low or zero debt, and positive cash flow metrics to be effective.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: A single point-in-time snapshot for balance sheet items and a full period (e.g., full year) for flow metrics.

ideal_for: When reassuring investors about the company's stability during a market downturn.
When you've just reached a major financial milestone like cash flow positivity.
To counter narratives about high burn rates or the need for future financing.
In a late-stage or pre-IPO pitch to prove the business is self-sustaining.
To signal strength and the ability to make strategic acquisitions or investments.
When shifting the company story from pure growth to profitable, durable growth.
avoid_when: When the company has high debt or a weak cash position.
When cash flow is negative and the story is about growth at all costs.
For very early-stage companies where the focus is on product and traction, not balance sheet.

records.title: Adjusted Free Cash Flow and Cash From Operations

records.core_message: We are making a deliberate strategic trade-off, accepting a lower operating margin in the short term to fund business expansion, while still maintaining substantial profitability.

shows.specific_content: A bar chart comparing Adjusted Operating Income and Adjusted Operating Margin for fiscal years 2021 and 2022. The chart shows a decrease in both the absolute income and the margin percentage from the prior year.
shows.data_points_shown: FY 2021: $473M Adjusted Operating Income, 31% Margin. FY 2022: $421M Adjusted Operating Income, 22% Margin.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern is used to proactively address a decline in a key profitability or efficiency metric. It presents the data transparently but frames the decrease as a deliberate, strategic choice to invest in long-term growth. Any company can use this when a key ratio (like margin or sales efficiency) temporarily dips due to planned investments in expansion, R&D, or market entry. The goal is to turn a potentially negative signal into a positive one about responsible, forward-looking management, demonstrating a commitment to fiscal responsibility even while making growth-oriented trade-offs.
works_for: Our customer acquisition cost has temporarily increased as we enter a new, larger market.
We are intentionally increasing R&D spend, which impacts near-term EBITDA, to build our next-generation platform.
Our gross margins have slightly decreased as we launched a lower-margin product to capture a wider audience.
While our free cash flow is lower this year, it's because we made a significant strategic acquisition to accelerate our roadmap.
Our sales efficiency dipped this quarter as we onboarded a large new sales team that will drive future growth.
We are sacrificing some near-term profitability to aggressively gain market share.
The drop in our contribution margin is a direct result of our successful international expansion efforts.

variable_elements.primary_metric: An absolute financial metric (e.g., Operating Income, EBITDA, Free Cash Flow)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A related efficiency or ratio metric (e.g., Operating Margin, Gross Margin, Sales Efficiency)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time

must_have: Time-series data for an absolute profitability/cash flow metric
Time-series data for a related efficiency/margin metric
A clear, defensible reason for the decline in the efficiency metric
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a decrease or flattening in the efficiency/ratio metric between two periods, while the absolute metric remains substantial or positive.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 2+ time periods (e.g., two years, two quarters)

ideal_for: Explaining a planned dip in profitability or efficiency to investors.
Justifying increased spending on growth initiatives like R&D, sales, or market expansion.
Shifting the narrative from short-term margin pressure to long-term strategic investment.
Demonstrating mature, proactive financial management in a public or late-stage company.
When you need to get ahead of a potentially negative financial story and control the narrative.
avoid_when: The decline in margins is unplanned or a sign of poor execution.
You cannot clearly articulate the strategic investment that caused the decline.
The absolute profitability number is also weak, negative, or rapidly deteriorating.

records.title: Adjusted Operating Income and Margin

records.core_message: We are providing clear, confident financial guidance for the upcoming quarter and full year, projecting strong revenue growth and sustained profitability.

shows.specific_content: Two panels display forward-looking financial guidance. The left panel shows full-year (FY 2023) expectations for Revenue, Adjusted Income from Operations, and GAAP Net Income. The right panel shows first-quarter (Q1 2023) expectations for Revenue and Adjusted Income from Operations. All quantitative figures are presented as ranges.
shows.data_points_shown: FY 2023 Guidance: Revenue ($2.18B - $2.23B), Adjusted Income ($481M - $531M), GAAP Net Income (mentioned as a target). Q1 2023 Guidance: Revenue ($503M - $507M), Adjusted Income ($91M - $95M).

records.abstract_pattern: Any mature company can use this pattern to communicate its official financial forecast to investors and analysts. It involves presenting key performance indicators, typically revenue and a profitability metric, as projected ranges for both a near-term period (like the next quarter) and a longer-term period (like the full year). This side-by-side structure demonstrates both short-term execution and long-term visibility. Using ranges helps manage expectations and account for uncertainty, while the act of providing guidance itself signals confidence and maturity.
works_for: We are raising our full-year outlook based on strong Q1 performance.
Our forecast shows we will reach 10 million daily active users by year-end.
We expect to achieve positive free cash flow in the second half of the year.
Our guidance for the next quarter is $100M in revenue and a 10% EBITDA margin.
We project ARR will grow between 30-35% in the next fiscal year.
We are confident in our ability to expand gross margins to 75% by Q4.
Our bookings forecast for next year is between $50M and $55M.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A top-line metric (e.g., Revenue, Bookings, ARR, GMV)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A profitability or efficiency metric (e.g., Adjusted Income, EBITDA, Net Income, Free Cash Flow)
variable_elements.time_dimension: Future time periods (e.g., next quarter, next year)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Near-term outlook vs. longer-term outlook

must_have: A robust financial model for forecasting future revenue and expenses
Management consensus on achievable targets
Historical data to inform the forecast model
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: forecasted_range
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: Forecasts for at least two key metrics (e.g., top-line and bottom-line) across two future time periods (e.g., quarter and year).

ideal_for: In an earnings call presentation to set expectations for the market.
To demonstrate confidence and visibility into the business's future performance.
As a public or late-stage private company aiming to build credibility with financial analysts.
When you need to formally communicate financial targets to investors and the board.
To signal a transition to a more predictable, mature business model.
avoid_when: When your business is highly unpredictable and forecasting is unreliable.
In an early-stage pitch where the focus is on vision and market size, not precise financials.
If there is a high risk of missing the targets, which would severely damage credibility.
